{
    "content": "<p>I'm doing research to better understand the padding oracle attack that was\nrecently disclosed to affect ASP.NET and thought to provide a quick list of\nlinks that I've found most helpful:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"http://blogs.msdn.com/b/sharepoint/archive/2010/09/21/security-advisory-2416728-vulnerability-in-asp-net-and-sharepoint.aspx\">Microsoft SharePoint Team Blog: Security Advisory 2416728 (Vulnerability in ASP.NET) and SharePoint</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"http://www.gdssecurity.com/l/b/2010/09/14/automated-padding-oracle-attacks-with-padbuster/\">Automated Padding Oracle Attacks with PadBuster</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"http://www.acunetix.com/blog/news/check-application-vulnerable-asp-net-padding-oracle-vulnerability/\">How to check if your application is vulnerable to the ASP.NET Padding Oracle Vulnerability</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"http://forums.asp.net/p/1604549/4090643.aspx\">Duncan Smart's post on ASP.NET detailing how to check if your application masks the oracle</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"http://blog.dotsmart.net/2010/09/22/asp-net-padding-oracle-detector/\">Duncan Smart's blog entry on the matter (with link to a wsh script to use for testing)</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"http://forums.asp.net/t/1604739.aspx\">ASP.NET forum post dealing with classic ASP. Guess what - your ASP site may be vulnerable if you haven't disabled some ASP.NET features</a></li>\n</ul>\n<p>The ASP Classic is the most unexpected bit to me, but makes perfect sense.</p>\n<p>Update: Patch your servers, as the padding oracle is\n<a href=\"http://blog.mindedsecurity.com/2010/10/breaking-net-encryption-with-or-without.html\">no longer needed</a>.\nThanks Matt!</p>\n",
